subject: PyStan: Boost exception with custom init

messages.author: 22d6bf0e16759db6
messages.subject: PyStan: Boost exception with custom init
parts:
I'm getting the following error when I add parameter initialization to a pystan.stan call:

terminate called after throwing an instance of 'boost::exception_detail::clone_impl<boost::exception_detail::error_info_injector<boost::bad_lexical_cast> >'

This happens after compilation is complete and it's trying to run the model, so I think it has to do with how pystan is packaging up the initialization dict and shipping it off to the compiled model (utility functions in stanfit4model.pyx ?).

The details...

pystan.__version__
'2.6.3.0'

% python --version
Python 2.7.9 :: Anaconda 2.0.1 (x86_64)

% cc --version
Apple LLVM version 6.1.0 (clang-602.0.53) (based on LLVM 3.6.0svn)
Target: x86_64-apple-darwin14.4.0
Thread model: posix


And here's a minimal example that works fine before you add initialization:

import pystan

model_code = '''
data { }
parameters { real mu; }
model { mu ~ normal(0, 1); }
'''

fit = pystan.stan(
    data = {},
    model_code = model_code,
    iter = 2000,
    warmup = 1000,
    chains = 1,
    n_jobs = 1
)



If I then add this initialization function:

def init_params(chain_id=1):
    return {'mu' : 0.1}

and change the stan call to this:

fit = pystan.stan(
    data = {},
    model_code = model_code,
    iter = 2000,
    warmup = 1000,
    chains = 1,
    n_jobs = 1,
    init = init_params
)

then I get the error. I get the same result if I remove the chain_id kwarg from the function.

Any ideas? 

And one other related issue: the PyStan documentation implies that you should instead be able to write a function that returns a list of dicts, e.g. for one chain, something like this:

def init_params():
    return [{'mu' : 0.1}]

but you get an exception:

ValueError: The function specifying initial values must return a dictionary.

This list-of-dicts option seems like an unnecessary feature anyway--might as well just take it out of the docs.

Ed

messages.author: f4c2e63aec3c6db2
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] PyStan: Boost exception with custom init
parts:
Hi Ed,

The function one passes as the `init` argument needs to accept a chain
id argument and return a dictionary of parameters. So the following will
work

def init_params(chain_id):
return {'mu': 0.1}

Alternatively you can explicitly provide the initial parameters for each
chain:

In [12]: init_list = [{'mu': 0.1}] * 4

In [13]: init_list
Out[13]: [{'mu': 0.1}, {'mu': 0.1}, {'mu': 0.1}, {'mu': 0.1}]

In [14]: fit = sm.sampling(data={}, iter=200, chains=4, n_jobs=1, init=init_list)

I hope this helps!

Best wishes,

Allen

> return [{'mu' : 0.1}]
